disease_label_per_paper: Severe diabetic ketoacidosis with severe hypokalemia and persistent hypernatremia in an adolescent girl with COVID-19 infection
presentation_summary: 13-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with excessive tiredness for 48 hours after a 9-week history of polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss.

Physical examination showed severe dehydration with poor skin turgor and delayed capillary refill of 3 seconds, deep Kussmaul breathing, tachycardia 126/min, intermittent bradycardia 40-50/min, and normal neurologic exam with GCS 15/15.

Initial labs showed glucose 32 mmol/L, blood ketones 7 mmol/L, venous pH 7.06, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess -22.6, potassium 1.9 mmol/L, corrected sodium 134 mmol/L, WBC 23.9 x 10^9/L, platelets 626 x 10^9/L, CRP <4 mg/L, urea 5.8 mmol/L, and creatinine 74 micromol/L.
Admission nasopharyngeal swab returned positive for COVID-19, but she remained asymptomatic from COVID-19 during admission; this trigger confirmation is kept non-ranking.

risk_context.source_text_value: long-lasting polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss for 9 weeks

observations.source_text_value: previously fit and well; no family history; long polyuria/polydipsia/weight loss prodrome
excessive tiredness for the last 48 h
weight loss, particularly marked during the 9 weeks preceding admission
severe dehydration with poor skin turgor and delayed capillary refill time 3 s
intermittent bouts of bradycardia 40-50/minute with severe hypokalemia
neurological examination at admission was normal with GCS 15/15

course_observations.source_text_value: on arrival in PICU, pH dropped further to 6.9
potassium had slightly improved to 2.2 mmol/L

confirmatory_findings.finding: Clinical and laboratory findings consistent with severe DKA
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Clinical and laboratory findings were consistent with severe DKA.
routine nasopharyngeal swab for COVID-19 returned a positive polymerase chain reaction result
She remained asymptomatic from the COVID-19 infection throughout the admission.

actual_treatment: central line for higher potassium replacement
insulin infusion delayed until potassium reached 2.5 mmol/L
hypertonic saline for cerebral edema concern

outcome.clinical_course: Transferred to PICU for persistent hypokalemia and cerebral edema concern; initial insulin was delayed due to severe hypokalemia.
outcome.source_text_value: Insulin infusion was started 15 h after admission after potassium improved; subsequent course included persistent acidosis and neurologic concern.

quality_warnings: COVID PCR and trigger attribution are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Treatment-period worsening pH, hypernatremia, and potassium trajectory are course observations with use_in_ranking:false.
Initial severe hypokalemia is rankable because it is a presentation lab, but treatment response is not used as diagnostic evidence.
